name: Tolterodine BOO Safety
question: Does tolterodine alter pressure-flow measurements or urinary retention over 12 weeks in men with overactive bladder and urodynamic bladder outlet obstruction?

design.population: Men older than 40 years with overactive bladder, urodynamically confirmed detrusor overactivity, and bladder outlet obstruction.

verdictNote: Primary urodynamic comparisons lack a reported prespecified safety margin; retention events were sparse.
takeaway: In men with urodynamic bladder outlet obstruction and detrusor overactivity, tolterodine versus placebo produced comparable flow and voiding-pressure measurements over 12 weeks. Postvoid residual rose more with tolterodine; the only reported urinary retention event was on placebo.

reports.label: Primary urodynamic safety report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give March 2006; day imputed for timeline
reports.citation: Abrams P, Kaplan S, De Koning Gans HJ, et al. "Safety and tolerability of tolterodine for the treatment of overactive bladder in men with bladder outlet obstruction." *J Urol.* 2006;175(3 Pt 1):999-1004. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)00483-0

results.measure: Median between-group difference in maximum urinary flow rate, mL/s
results.note: The abstract reports no prespecified safety or noninferiority margin.

results.measure: Median between-group difference in detrusor pressure at maximum flow, cm H2O
results.note: The abstract prints a 95% CI of -3 to 11, which does not contain its reported -7 estimate; interval omitted pending full text.

results.measure: Change in bladder outlet obstruction index
Between-group difference in volume to first detrusor contraction, mL
Between-group difference in maximum cystometric capacity, mL
Change in postvoid residual volume, mL

harms.label: Reported urinary retention
harms.note: The abstract reports one retention event on placebo and none on tolterodine; it does not define catheterization or adjudication.

values.exp: Tolterodine 2 mg twice daily for 12 weeks
